extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors reporting in vivo animal experiments; peer reviewers and journal editors assessing animal-study manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors and reviewers on what to report in manuscripts describing in vivo (animal) experiments to ensure transparency, reproducibility, and assessment of reliability. The document is organised into an Essential 10 minimum reporting items and a Recommended Set of supplementary items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of the overall study design sufficient for readers/reviewers to assess validity and reproducibility (e.g., experimental groups, controls, experimental unit, timing/sequence of procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the ARRIVE Essential 10 (a basic minimum). The site provides examples of good reporting drawn from the literature. Consult this item during study planning to improve design and reduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Report how sample sizes were decided, including any a priori calculations, rationale, and the number of experimental units per group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Examples of appropriate reporting are provided. Accurate sample size reporting is needed for assessment of reliability and statistical power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify criteria used to include or exclude animals or data points, and describe any exclusions (with reasons) and how they were handled in the analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the ARRIVE Essential 10. The guidelines include illustrative examples; transparent inclusion/exclusion reporting reduces bias and improves reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods used to allocate animals or experimental units to groups (randomisation or other allocation methods) to minimise selection bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Examples of good reporting are provided. Clear reporting of allocation methods is necessary for evaluating internal validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding/Masking
rubrics_metrics.description: State who was blinded (or masked) to group allocation at different stages (e.g., during conduct of experiment, outcome assessment, and data analysis) and, if not blinded, provide a rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Examples are included on the website. Reporting blinding practices helps assess risk of detection/performance bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Define all outcome measures (primary and secondary), how and when they were measured, and any criteria for measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the ARRIVE Essential 10. The site gives examples of good reporting. Clear specification of outcomes allows correct interpretation and synthesis of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the statistical methods used for each analysis, including the unit of analysis, any assumptions checked, and software/packages used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Examples of appropriate statistical reporting are provided. Complete reporting supports evaluation of analytic rigor and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details about the animals used (species, strain, substrain, sex, age or developmental stage, weight, provenance, genetic status, health/immune status, and any previous procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Examples from the literature illustrate good reporting. Detailed animal descriptions are essential for reproducibility and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe procedures in sufficient detail to allow replication (what was done, how, when, where, and why), including drugs, dosages, routes, surgical procedures, equipment and any specialist training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the ARRIVE Essential 10. The guidelines include exemplar descriptions. Thorough procedural detail enables replication and assessment of welfare impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.description: Report results for all outcome measures, including summary/descriptive statistics, measures of variability/precision (e.g., SD, CI), effect sizes, and exact p-values where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Examples are provided. Complete and transparent result reporting is required for assessing reliability and for meta-analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an accurate and balanced summary of the objectives, methods, key results, and conclusions in the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set. Examples of good abstracts are supplied. A clear abstract helps readers quickly assess relevance and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the scientific background and rationale for the study, including relevant literature and the knowledge gap addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set. The site provides examples. Background contextualises objectives and helps assess justification for the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: State the specific objectives, hypotheses, or research questions the study aims to address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set. Examples are included. Clear objectives enable evaluation of whether the study design and analyses are aligned with the aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of ethical oversight, approvals, licences, and any relevant welfare-related statements or regulations followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set. Examples and explanatory text are provided. Ethical transparency is required for assessing compliance and welfare considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.description: Report housing and husbandry conditions (e.g., cage type, bedding, number/grouping of animals, light/dark cycle, temperature, diet, enrichment) that could influence outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set. Examples from published studies are given. Housing details inform generalisability and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe monitoring during the experiment, husbandry practices for welfare, interventions used for pain or distress, and predefined humane endpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set. The site includes illustrative reporting. Monitoring and care reporting are important for ethical evaluation and understanding potential impacts on data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation/ scientific implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the interpretation of results, considering study limitations, sources of potential bias, and the broader scientific implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set. Examples and explanatory notes are provided. Honest interpretation supports correct inference and responsible translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability/ translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the generalisability of findings to other species, strains, or to clinical/human contexts, and any limitations to translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set. The guidelines supply examples. Consideration of generalisability aids readers in judging applicability of the findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the study protocol (including hypotheses, methods, and analysis plan) was pre-registered and provide registration details or a rationale if not registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set. Examples and discussion are provided. Protocol registration increases transparency and reduces risk of selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a data availability statement specifying where study data, code, and materials can be accessed (or explain restrictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set. The site gives examples. Data access facilitates reproducibility, secondary analysis, and meta-research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose all funding sources, competing interests, and any other declarations that could influence study design, conduct, or reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set. Examples and explanatory text are provided. Full disclosure supports assessment of potential bias or conflicts.
